title: Personal Checking: Early Closure Fee, Inactivity Period and Dormant Account Fee
content:
Personal Checking attaches two tier figures to closing an account soon after opening it, and two to an account that falls idle.

- **Early closure fee (USD)** — the charge an owner pays for shutting the account down while it is still inside the early closure window.
- **Early closure window (calendar days)** — the number of calendar days after the opening date during which an owner-initiated closure draws the early closure fee.
- **Inactivity period (calendar months)** — how many months may pass with no activity started by the customer before the account is classed as dormant.
- **Dormant account fee (USD)** — the cycle-by-cycle charge on an idle account, trimmed where needed so the balance stops at zero.

| Tier | Early closure fee | Early closure window | Inactivity period | Dormant account fee |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Access Checking | 0.00 | 90 | 12 | 0.00 |
| Student Checking | 0.00 | 90 | 12 | 0.00 |
| Everyday Checking | 25.00 | 90 | 12 | 5.00 |
| Interest Checking | 25.00 | 90 | 12 | 5.00 |
| Premier Checking | 25.00 | 90 | 12 | 5.00 |
| Private Client Checking | 25.00 | 90 | 24 | 0.00 |

## Pointers from the figures

- Private Client Checking is the only tier that waits 24 months before an idle account turns dormant, and it charges nothing while dormant.
- Access and Student Checking charge neither an early closure fee nor a dormant account fee.
- Hypothetical example: an Interest Checking account closed by its owner 90 calendar days after opening is still inside the 90-day window; one closed on day 91 is outside it.
